page: OVHcloud r2-240-flex is a memory-optimized cloud instance configured with 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running on x86_64 Intel Haswell architecture at 2.2 GHz. The instance features a 1-to-1 thread allocation without hyperthreading, alongside 240.0 GB of system memory, providing 15.0 GB of RAM per core. Hardware acceleration is not included, as the server has 0 GPUs. Attached storage is modest, consisting of a 50 GB local SSD, and the baseline network connection is rated at 10 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate contrasting single-core and multi-core capabilities attributable to the legacy CPU microarchitecture. Single-core performance falls in the lower tiers, reflected in a stress-ng single-core score of 871.59 and a Geekbench single-core result of 986.0. In contrast, multi-threaded workloads exhibit average results, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 5626.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 12999.31. Uncached memory bandwidth measures at 30.5 GB/sec for reads and 20.5 GB/sec for writes, which trails newer generations, though small cached read bandwidth remains capable at 839.34 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r2-240-flex trades raw per-core CPU execution speed for a very dense memory footprint. In-memory throughput is demonstrated by 11.94 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and a 10.25 GB/sec static web serving rate. However, modern compute-intensive tasks, such as 7B parameter LLM text generation at 6.13 tokens/sec, perform poorly due to the lack of modern vector extensions like AVX-512 or AMX.

Given its substantial 240.0 GB RAM capacity balanced against legacy CPU cores and small 50 GB local disk space, the r2-240-flex is best fitted for memory-intensive operational caching, distributed in-memory databases, memory-resident analytics, and large-scale ETL staging where RAM capacity dominates processing requirements.
